{{Short description|Class of algebraic theorems}}
'''Local rigidity''' theorems in the theory of discrete subgroups of [[Lie group]]s are results which show that small deformations of certain such subgroups are always trivial. It is different from [[Mostow rigidity]] and weaker (but holds more frequently) than [[superrigidity]].

== History ==

The first such theorem was proven by [[Atle Selberg]] for co-compact discrete subgroups of the unimodular groups <math>\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb R)</math>.<ref>{{cite book |  last1 = Selberg | first1 = Atle| author1-link=Atle Selberg  | title=Contributions to functional theory | year=1960 |publisher=Tata Institut, Bombay |pages=100–110 |chapter=On discontinuous groups in higher-dimensional symmetric spaces}}</ref> Shortly afterwards a similar statement was proven by [[Eugenio Calabi]] in the setting of fundamental groups of compact hyperbolic manifolds. Finally, the theorem was extended to all co-compact subgroups of semisimple Lie groups by [[André Weil]].<ref>{{Citation | last1=Weil | first1=André | author1-link=André Weil | title=On discrete subgroups of Lie groups | jstor=1970140 | mr=0137792 | year=1960 | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |series=Second Series | issn=0003-486X | volume=72 | issue=2 | pages=369–384 | doi=10.2307/1970140}}</ref><ref>{{Citation | last1=Weil | first1=André | author1-link=André Weil | title=On discrete subgroups of Lie groups. II | jstor=1970212 | mr=0137793 | year=1962 | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |series=Second Series | issn=0003-486X | volume=75 | issue=3 | pages=578–602 | doi=10.2307/1970212}}</ref> The extension to non-cocompact lattices was made later by Howard Garland and [[M. S. Raghunathan|Madabusi Santanam Raghunathan]].<ref>{{cite journal

The result is now sometimes referred to as Calabi—Weil (or just Weil) rigidity.

== Statement ==

=== Deformations of subgroups ===

Let <math>\Gamma</math> be a group [[Generating set of a group|generated]] by a finite number of elements <math>g_1, \ldots, g_n</math> and <math>G</math> a Lie group. Then the map <math>\mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma, G) \to G^n</math> defined by <math> \rho \mapsto (\rho(g_1), \ldots, \rho(g_n))</math> is injective and this endows <math>\mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma, G)</math> with a topology [[Induced topology|induced]] by that of <math>G^n</math>. If <math>\Gamma</math> is a subgroup of <math>G</math> then a ''deformation'' of <math>\Gamma</math> is any element in <math>\mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma, G)</math>. Two representations <math>\phi, \psi</math> are said to be conjugated if there exists a <math>g \in G</math> such that <math> \phi(\gamma) = g\psi(\gamma) g^{-1} </math> for all <math> \gamma \in \Gamma</math>. See also [[character variety]].

=== Lattices in simple groups not of type A1 or A1 &times; A1===

The simplest statement is when <math>\Gamma</math> is a lattice in a simple Lie group <math>G</math> and the latter is not locally isomorphic to <math>\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)</math> or <math>\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)</math> and <math>\Gamma</math> (this means that its Lie algebra is not that of one of these two groups).

:''There exists a neighbourhood <math>U</math> in <math>\mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma, G)</math> of the inclusion <math>i : \Gamma \subset G</math> such that any <math>\phi \in U</math> is conjugated to <math>i</math>. ''

Whenever such a statement holds for a pair <math>G \supset \Gamma</math> we will say that local rigidity holds.

=== Lattices in SL(2,C) ===

Local rigidity holds for cocompact lattices in <math>\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)</math>. A lattice <math>\Gamma</math> in <math>\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)</math> which is not cocompact has nontrivial deformations coming from Thurston's [[hyperbolic Dehn surgery]] theory. However, if one adds the restriction that a representation must send parabolic elements in <math>\Gamma</math> to parabolic elements then local rigidity holds.

=== Lattices in SL(2,R) ===

In this case local rigidity never holds (except [[Cocompact group action | cocompact]] [[Triangle groups #The hyperbolic case | triangle groups]]). For cocompact lattices a small deformation remains a cocompact lattice but it may not be conjugated to the original one (see [[Teichmüller space]] for more detail). Non-cocompact lattices are virtually free and hence have non-lattice deformations.

=== Semisimple Lie groups ===

Local rigidity holds for lattices in [[Simple_Lie_group#Semisimple_Lie_groups | semisimple Lie groups]] providing the latter have no factor of type A1 (i.e. locally isomorphic to <math>\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)</math> or <math>\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)</math>) or the former is irreducible.

== Other results ==

There are also local rigidity results where the ambient group is changed, even in case where superrigidity fails. For example, if <math>\Gamma</math> is a lattice in the [[unitary group]] <math>\mathrm{SU}(n,1)</math> and <math>n \ge 2</math> then the inclusion <math>\Gamma \subset \mathrm{SU}(n,1) \subset \mathrm{SU}(n+1,1)</math> is locally rigid.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Goldman | first1=William | author1-link = William Goldman | last2=Millson | first2=John | author2-link = John Millson (mathematician) | title=Local rigidity of discrete groups acting on complex hyperbolic space  | year=1987 | journal=Inventiones Mathematicae | volume=88 | issue=3 | pages=495–520 | doi=10.1007/bf01391829| bibcode=1987InMat..88..495G | s2cid=15347622 }}</ref>

A uniform lattice <math>\Gamma</math> in any compactly generated topological group <math>G</math> is ''topologically locally rigid'', in the sense that any sufficiently small deformation <math>\varphi</math> of the inclusion <math>i : \Gamma \subset G</math> is injective and <math>\varphi(\Gamma)</math> is a uniform lattice in <math>G</math>. An irreducible uniform lattice in the isometry group of any proper geodesically complete <math>\mathrm{CAT}(0)</math>-space  not isometric to the hyperbolic plane and without Euclidean factors is locally rigid.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Gelander| first1=Tsachik | author1-link = Tsachik Gelander | last2=Levit | first2=Arie | title=Local rigidity of uniform lattices  | year=2017| journal= [[Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici]] | arxiv= 1605.01693 }}</ref>

== Proofs of the theorem ==

Weil's original proof is by relating deformations of a subgroup <math>\Gamma</math> in <math>G</math> to the first [[Group cohomology|cohomology]] group of <math>\Gamma</math> with coefficients in the Lie algebra of <math>G</math>, and then showing that this cohomology vanishes for cocompact lattices when <math>G</math> has no simple factor of absolute type A1. A more geometric proof which also work in the non-compact cases uses [[Charles Ehresmann]] (and [[William Thurston]]'s) theory of <math>(G, X)</math> structures.<ref>{{cite journal
